title: LLM Semantic Clustering for Polymarket Pair Arbitrage (Same-Outcome Links)
source: arXiv:2512.02436 (Dec 2025) — "Semantic Trading: Agentic AI for Clustering and Trading of Prediction Markets"
summary: arXiv:2512.02436 introduces a two-stage agentic pipeline for prediction market arbitrage: (1) an LLM clusters Polymarket contracts by semantic content (contract text + metadata), identifying same-outcome links (correlated resolution) and different-outcome links (anti-correlated resolution); (2) trades are placed when linked contracts show price divergence — buying the underpriced contract in a same-outcome pair when its linked partner is priced higher. Performance: 60-70% accuracy in predicting relational patterns; ~20% average returns over week-long horizons on resolved Polymarket contracts. Distinction from cointegration: semantic clustering discovers implicit logical relationships ('Will the Fed cut in March?' and 'Will the 2Y yield drop below 4% by April?' are logically linked) that price history alone cannot identify. Relevance: this directly extends the prediction markets work (H185 nowcasting, automated-pipeline.md). A production implementation would: (1) pull active Polymarket contracts via the CLOB API, (2) embed contract descriptions using text-embedding-3-small, (3) cluster using cosine similarity threshold > 0.80, (4) identify same-outcome pairs where |price_A - price_B| > 5%, (5) buy the cheaper leg with Kelly sizing. Key risk: Polymarket contracts may have different resolution dates, liquidity, or event dependencies that create false 'same-outcome' classifications. Requires careful validation before capital commitment. Implementation cost: ~$5-10/month OpenAI embedding API for nightly batch. This is a wiki update + design note, not a backtest.
